name: Ridley Scott
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; directed student short film 'Boy and Bicycle' at age 22-23 at the Royal College of Art, but first feature film 'The Duellists' did not arrive until age 39 in 1977.

name: Yelena Isinbayeva
milestone_by_age_26: Set her first outdoor world record of 4.82m in the women's pole vault at the Norwich Union Super Grand Prix in Gateshead on July 13, 2003, at age 21, and went on to win Olympic gold at age 22 in 2004.
early_history_summary: Born to a working-class family in Volgograd, Isinbayeva trained as a gymnast from age 5 but was redirected to pole vault at 15 for being too tall. Under coach Yevgeny Trofimov, she progressed rapidly, winning the World Youth Games in 1998 and World Junior title in 2000, before breaking the senior world record at 21.
family_context_summary: Born to a Tabasaran father who worked as a plumber and a Russian mother who was a shop assistant; the family made significant financial sacrifices to support her early career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not involved in athletics; mother had amateur basketball interest but no professional sports background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: dedicated coach, gymnastics background, Olympic reserve school, training peers, emerging event
evidence_summary: Isinbayeva came from humble beginnings in Volgograd with parents who made financial sacrifices for her career. Her gymnastics training from age 5 to 15 provided a physical foundation, and coach Yevgeny Trofimov's sustained mentorship from age 15 transformed her into a world-record pole vaulter by 21. She trained alongside World and Olympic champions Lebedeva and Slesarenko at the Volgograd sports school. Women's pole vault was an emerging event, which may have lowered the barrier to rapid ascent.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Volgograd; father was a Tabasaran plumber and mother a shop assistant who made financial sacrifices for her career.
current_position: Retired from athletics in 2016 after being banned from Rio Olympics due to Russian doping scandal; elected to IOC Athletes' Commission; resides in Russia.

trajectory.event: Won World Youth Games in pole vault, six months after taking up the sport.
Set first outdoor world record of 4.82m at the Norwich Union Super Grand Prix in Gateshead.
Won Olympic gold medal in Athens and set multiple world records; named World Athlete of the Year.
Became first woman to clear 5 meters; won World Championship gold in Helsinki.
Won second Olympic gold medal in Beijing with a world record of 5.05m.
Set current outdoor world record of 5.06m in Zürich.
Retired from athletics after being banned from Rio Olympics; elected to IOC Athletes' Commission.

name: Niklas Landin Jacobsen
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2012 European Championship with Denmark at age 23, having already made his senior international debut at 19 and established himself as a top professional goalkeeper.
early_history_summary: Born in Søborg, Denmark, Landin Jacobsen was exposed to handball from age 3 through his parents' involvement in the KFUM handball club. He progressed through youth ranks at KFUM København and GOG, signed a senior contract with GOG Svendborg TGI at 17, and made his Denmark national team debut at 19, becoming European champion by 23.
family_context_summary: Grew up in a stable suburban Copenhagen family; parents were actively involved in the KFUM handball club, creating a household environment that emphasized community sport and physical activity.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were involved in the KFUM handball club in Copenhagen, providing early exposure to the sport and a community sports environment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: handball from age 3, parents in club, Danish handball culture, Oure sports school, GOG pipeline, brother Magnus, Gudmundsson mentor
evidence_summary: Landin Jacobsen grew up in a Danish suburban family deeply embedded in the KFUM handball community, with parents actively involved in the club. He was exposed to handball from age 3 and progressed through the Danish youth system, including Oure Idrætsefterskole and the GOG pipeline. His younger brother Magnus also became an elite handball player. Coach Gudmundur Gudmundsson gave him the starting goalkeeper role at GOG at age 17-18, accelerating his development. Denmark's strong handball culture and grassroots infrastructure provided a fertile ecosystem.
starting_point: Born in Søborg, a suburb of Copenhagen, Denmark; parents were actively involved in the KFUM handball club, providing a stable sporting environment from childhood.
current_position: Plays for Aalborg Håndbold; two-time IHF World Player of the Year (2019, 2021); widely regarded as one of the greatest handball goalkeepers ever; retired from international play in 2024.

trajectory.event: Signed senior professional contract with GOG Svendborg TGI, beginning top-level club career.
Made senior international debut for Denmark national team on October 28 against Austria.
Won European Championship with Denmark; named Danish Handballer of the Year.
Won EHF Cup with Rhein-Neckar Löwen in his first season at the German club.
Won Olympic gold medal with Denmark at the Rio Olympics.
Won World Championship with Denmark and named IHF World Player of the Year for the first time.
Won EHF Champions League with THW Kiel.
Won second Olympic gold at Paris Olympics; retired from international team duty.

name: Madeleine Berthod
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in the women's downhill at the 1956 Cortina d'Ampezzo Winter Olympics on her 25th birthday, winning by 4.7 seconds, the largest margin in the event's history.
early_history_summary: Born to a farming family in Château-d'Oex, Switzerland, Berthod skied to school in winter and worked on the family farm. She won her first regional championship at 13 in 1944, her first Swiss national title at 21 in 1952, and World Championship silver medals at 23 in 1954 before her Olympic triumph at 25.
family_context_summary: Raised in a farming family in Château-d'Oex, Vaud; she milked cows and made butter while training, with her parents operating a farm near one of the first ski lifts in the canton.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were farmers with no documented connection to competitive skiing; the local Alpine environment provided natural access to the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swiss Alps upbringing, early ski lift, skied to school, farming hardship, beat boys at 13
evidence_summary: Berthod grew up on a farm in Château-d'Oex with one of the first ski lifts in the canton of Vaud, giving her rare early access to the sport. She skied to school in winter and was discovered by the Ski Club de Château-d'Oex after regularly beating boys, sending her to regional championships at 13. The farming family had modest means, and she balanced farm work with ski training. No dedicated coach or elite academy was documented; her advantage came from geographic immersion in the Swiss Alps.
starting_point: Born to a farming family in Château-d'Oex, Vaud, Switzerland; grew up working on the family farm and skiing to school in winter.
current_position: Living as Switzerland's oldest living Olympic champion at age 94; resides in Switzerland.

trajectory.event: Won the Championnats romands ski competition, her first notable competitive result.
Won first of six Swiss national championships and competed at Oslo Olympics, placing 6th in downhill and slalom.
Won two silver medals in giant slalom and combined at the FIS Alpine World Ski Championships in Åre, Sweden.
Won Olympic gold in downhill at Cortina d'Ampezzo on her 25th birthday by 4.7 seconds; named Swiss Sports Personality of the Year.
Competed at Squaw Valley Olympics, finishing 9th in giant slalom, then retired from competition.

name: Mike Harrington
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; at age 26 he was a programmer at Microsoft working on Windows NT. He co-founded Valve at age 31-32 in 1996 and shipped Half-Life at age 34 in 1998. Note: CSV lists birth_year as 2000, but Wikipedia and multiple sources confirm birth year 1964.

name: Gisele Bündchen
milestone_by_age_26: Cast in Alexander McQueen's 1998 runway show at age 18, appeared on her first British Vogue cover, and was dubbed 'the Body' by McQueen, launching her as the face that ended the heroin chic era of modeling.
early_history_summary: Discovered at age 13-14 in a shopping mall in Brazil after her mother enrolled her in a modeling course, Bündchen moved to São Paulo at 15 and debuted at New York Fashion Week at 16. After being rejected 42 times in London, her 1998 McQueen show breakthrough catapulted her to supermodel status, leading to a Victoria's Secret Angel contract at 19 and a record $25M deal at 20.
family_context_summary: Born to a modest family in Horizontina, Brazil; father was a university professor with multiple jobs and mother a bank clerk; grew up with five sisters in a two-bedroom house for eight people.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents had no connection to the fashion industry; mother enrolled Gisele and her sisters in a modeling course to teach confidence and posture, which indirectly led to discovery.
primary_early_advantage_tags: distinctive physique, end of heroin chic, Elite Model Management, Brazilian model wave, twin sister Patricia, teased for being tall
evidence_summary: Bündchen grew up in modest circumstances in rural Brazil with no family connection to fashion. Her mother's decision to enroll her in a modeling course led to discovery by Elite Model Management at 13-14. Her distinctive physique (tall, curvy) was the antithesis of the heroin chic aesthetic and catalyzed a structural shift in the fashion industry. She was rejected 42 times before McQueen cast her, showing perseverance. Her twin sister Patricia became her long-time manager. The Brazilian model wave of the late 1990s provided a favorable geographic context.
starting_point: Born to a modest family in Horizontina, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil; father was a university professor and mother a bank clerk, sixth-generation German Brazilian with five sisters.
current_position: Retired from runway modeling in 2015; one of the world's highest-paid models with estimated net worth of ~$400M; resides in Miami, Florida.

trajectory.event: Debuted at New York Fashion Week, launching her international modeling career.
Cast in Alexander McQueen runway show; appeared on first British Vogue cover; dubbed 'the Body' by McQueen.
Became Victoria's Secret Angel; appeared on first US Vogue cover; credited with ending heroin chic era.
Signed record-breaking $25 million Victoria's Secret contract; named 'Most Beautiful Girl in the World' by Rolling Stone.
Named world's highest-paid model by Forbes, a title she would hold for multiple consecutive years.
Retired from runway modeling after final São Paulo Fashion Week appearance.
Divorced Tom Brady after 13 years of marriage.

name: Vladimir Bagirov
milestone_by_age_26: Finished 4th at the 1960 USSR Championship in Leningrad at age 23, defeating Korchnoi, Spassky, and Bronstein, and fulfilling his first grandmaster norm in his debut at the highest level of Soviet chess.
early_history_summary: Born in Baku to an Armenian father (arrested and shot in 1937) and a Ukrainian mother, Bagirov learned chess at age 10 at the Baku Pioneers' Palace under Suran Abramian. He came under the wing of master Vladimir Makogonov, earned the Soviet Master title at 22, and stunned the chess world with his 4th-place debut at the 1960 USSR Championship.
family_context_summary: Born to an Armenian father who was a prominent oil specialist arrested and shot in 1937, and a Ukrainian mother; Bagirov grew up fatherless in Baku and later trained as an engineer in the oil industry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an oil specialist with no documented connection to chess; no family domain advantage in the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Baku Pioneers Palace, Makogonov mentorship, Soviet chess pipeline, Baku chess city, fatherless, Abramian early teacher
evidence_summary: Bagirov grew up fatherless in Baku after his father was arrested and shot in 1937. He learned chess at 10 through the Baku Pioneers' Palace, a Soviet institutional pipeline, under teacher Suran Abramian. Master Vladimir Makogonov provided sustained mentorship that shaped his positional style. Baku was a major chess center that later produced Garry Kasparov. The Soviet chess system provided elite competition and training infrastructure. His 4th-place finish at the 1960 USSR Championship, defeating multiple grandmasters, was a remarkable debut achievement.
starting_point: Born in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR to an Armenian father (a prominent oil specialist arrested and shot in 1937) and a Ukrainian mother; grew up fatherless in Baku.
current_position: Died on July 21, 2000 at age 63 in Jyväskylä, Finland; suffered a heart attack during a tournament game; final role as Latvian chess grandmaster and trainer.

trajectory.event: Made debut in semi-finals of Soviet Championship but did not advance to the final.
Earned title of Soviet Master of Sport by defeating Yakov Estrin in a qualification match.
Finished 4th at USSR Championship in Leningrad, defeating Korchnoi, Spassky, and Bronstein; fulfilled first grandmaster norm.
Won European Team Championship with Soviet team and World Student Team Championship.
Awarded International Master title by FIDE.
Finally awarded Grandmaster title by FIDE after fulfilling second norm.
Won World Senior Chess Championship.
Died of a heart attack during a chess tournament in Jyväskylä, Finland.

name: Caetano Veloso
milestone_by_age_26: Released his debut album 'Domingo' with Gal Costa in 1967 at age 25, and co-founded the Tropicália movement with his self-titled solo album and the Tropicália compilation in 1968 at age 26, becoming a leading figure in Brazilian music.
early_history_summary: Born into a lower-middle-class family in Santo Amaro, Bahia, Veloso was immersed in music and arts from childhood, influenced by bossa nova and his sister Maria Bethânia, already a successful singer. He studied philosophy at the Federal University of Bahia, met Gilberto Gil and Gal Costa, won a lyric-writing contest, and moved to Rio in 1965 to launch his recording career.
family_context_summary: Born into a lower-middle-class family in Santo Amaro, Bahia; father was a postal employee and mother a homemaker with music and theatre training who strongly supported her children's artistic development; one of seven children.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother Dona Canô had received training in music and theatre and strongly supported artistic development of her children, particularly Caetano; sister Maria Bethânia was already a successful singer who helped open doors in the music industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: sister Maria Bethânia, Gilberto Gil, Gal Costa, Bahian music culture, mother's art support, Tropicália movement, military dictatorship
evidence_summary: Veloso grew up in a lower-middle-class family in Bahia immersed in music, with a mother who had music and theatre training and actively supported artistic development. His sister Maria Bethânia was already a successful singer, providing an inherited network into the music industry. At the Federal University of Bahia, he met Gilberto Gil and Gal Costa, forming an exceptional peer group that became the core of the Tropicália movement. Bahia was a cultural frontier for Brazilian music. The military dictatorship created adversity that shaped his artistic voice and eventually led to his exile.
starting_point: Born into a lower-middle-class family in Santo Amaro, Bahia, Brazil; father was a postal employee and mother a homemaker with music and theatre training who supported artistic development.
current_position: Active recording and performing artist at age 83; one of Brazil's most influential musicians with 19 Brazilian Music Awards, 9 Latin Grammys, and 2 Grammys.

trajectory.event: Moved to Rio de Janeiro to launch music career after winning a lyric-writing contest and being signed to Philips label.
Released debut album 'Domingo' with Gal Costa; began performing at televised music festivals.
Released self-titled solo album and the Tropicália compilation, co-founding the Tropicália movement.
Arrested by Brazilian military dictatorship and exiled to London for two years.
Returned to Brazil and resumed recording and performing.
Honored as Latin Recording Academy Person of the Year.

name: Quentin Tarantino
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; at 26 he was a video store clerk writing unsold screenplays. His directorial debut 'Reservoir Dogs' came at age 29 in 1992, and 'Pulp Fiction' at age 31 in 1994.

name: Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner
milestone_by_age_26: Climbed the fore-summit of Broad Peak (8,027m) in Pakistan at age 23, achieving her first 8000m peak while working as a nurse to fund her expeditions.
early_history_summary: Born in Kirchdorf an der Krems, Austria, Kaltenbrunner grew up in the small Alpine community of Spital am Pyhrn where a local minister, Reverend Dr. Erich Tischler, introduced her to mountaineering. She completed her first climbing tours at 13, pursued nurse training while honing her skills in the Alps, and achieved her dream of climbing an 8000m peak at 23.
family_context_summary: Grew up in the small resort community of Spital am Pyhrn in the Alps of central Austria; family background is not well documented beyond the local Alpine environment.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connection to mountaineering mentioned.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Austian Alps upbringing, Reverend Tischler mentor, climbing from age 13, nurse self-funding, Alpine culture
evidence_summary: Kaltenbrunner grew up in Spital am Pyhrn, a small Alpine community in Upper Austria, where local minister Reverend Dr. Erich Tischler introduced her to mountaineering after Sunday church services. She began climbing at 13 and developed skills through ski, ice, and rock climbing tours while training as a nurse. She self-funded her Himalayan expeditions with her nurse's salary. The geographic immersion in the Austrian Alps was the primary advantage, with no documented family wealth or elite institutional pipeline.
starting_point: Born in Kirchdorf an der Krems, Austria; grew up in the small Alpine community of Spital am Pyhrn where a local minister introduced her to mountaineering.
current_position: Professional mountaineer and speaker; first woman to climb all 14 eight-thousanders without supplemental oxygen; resides in Austria.

trajectory.event: Completed first climbing tours at local Sturzhahn, sparking her alpinism career.
Climbed fore-summit of Broad Peak (8,027m) in Pakistan, her first 8000m peak.
Summited Cho Oyu (8,188m), her first 8000m main summit.
Climbed Nanga Parbat, her fifth 8000m peak, and decided to pursue professional mountaineering full-time.
Became first woman to climb all 14 eight-thousanders without supplemental oxygen by summiting K2.
Won National Geographic Explorer of the Year Award.

name: Raymond Poulidor
milestone_by_age_26: Won Milan-San Remo, one of cycling's five Monuments, and the French national road championship in 1961 at age 25, his first major professional season after turning professional at 24.
early_history_summary: Born to sharecropping farmers in rural Creuse, France, Poulidor grew up in poverty during Nazi occupation, left school at 14 to work on the farm, and started racing at 16. After military service at 20, he was discovered by Tour de France winner Antoine Magne, turned professional with Mercier-BP at 24, and immediately won two major races in his debut season at 25.
family_context_summary: Born to Martial and Maria Poulidor, sharecropping farmers (métayers) in Masbaraud-Mérignat, Creuse; grew up in rural poverty during Nazi occupation with food shortages, left school at 14 to work on the farm.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were sharecropping farmers with no connection to cycling; older brothers raced bicycles recreationally, which inspired Poulidor to take up the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: rural poverty, sharecropping, Nazi occupation, older brothers racing, Mercier team, Magne discovery, farm labor
evidence_summary: Poulidor grew up in deep rural poverty as the son of sharecropping farmers in Creuse, France, during Nazi occupation. He left school at 14 to work on the farm and started racing at 16, inspired by his older brothers. After military service, he was discovered by Tour de France winner Antoine Magne, who connected him to the Mercier-BP professional team. The adversity of rural poverty and wartime hardship created a powerful drive. No family wealth, no elite academy, and no dedicated coach were documented; his path was one of constraint-driven self-creation through relentless riding.
starting_point: Born to sharecropping farmers in Masbaraud-Mérignat, Creuse, France; grew up in rural poverty during Nazi occupation, left school at 14 to work on the family farm.
current_position: Died on November 13, 2019 at age 83 in Saint-Léonard-de-Noblat, France; final status as French cycling legend known as 'The Eternal Second.'

trajectory.event: Turned professional with Mercier-BP-Hutchinson team after being discovered by Tour de France winner Antoine Magne.
Won Milan-San Remo and French national road championship in his first major professional season.
Won Vuelta a España and engaged in legendary duel with Jacques Anquetil on the Puy de Dôme at the Tour de France.
Won Critérium du Dauphiné Libéré and finished 3rd in Tour de France.
Finished 3rd in Tour de France at age 38, his final Tour podium.
Retired from professional cycling after 17-year career with Mercier.
Died on November 13 in Saint-Léonard-de-Noblat, France.

name: Ivan Marchuk
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; at 26 he was still a student at the Lviv Institute of Applied Arts, graduating at 29 in 1965. His first major recognition came in the 1970s with the invention of Pliontanism, and international attention in 1979.
